response.rationale: R5 is definitive: skin biopsy shows foamy histiocytes with numerous acid-fast bacilli, and the madarosis/eyelash-brow-beard-scalp hair loss with facial infiltration and nodules is classic lepromatous leprosy. R2 explains uveitis, lymphadenopathy/splenomegaly and nodules but cannot account for AFB and would require non-caseating granulomas. R4 explains joint swelling and elevated RF but is contradicted by normal anti-CCP and by the AFB-positive skin pathology.

rejected.why: Joint symptoms and elevated RF are nonspecific; normal anti-CCP and AFB-positive foamy histiocyte skin biopsy exclude rheumatoid arthritis as the primary diagnosis.
